lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hi Sam. What brings you in today?

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: He gets headaches most afternoons. It has been about three weeks.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sam, what do the headaches feel like?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They feel tight behind my eyes. They get worse after class.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Does anything help?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lying down in a dark room helps a little.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Why do I get these headaches?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your blood pressure looks normal today. I do not see a clear cause yet.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Please keep a headache diary for two weeks. Write down when it starts and how strong it is.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Can I have those instructions in writing?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. I will print them before you leave.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You can take ibuprofen if you need it. Follow the package directions.

lines.speaker: C
lines.text: I think the screen at school is [unclear] for him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Please come back in four weeks. Bring the diary with you.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Okay. Thank you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Book the follow-up at the front desk on your way out.
